transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because… since my grandson was killed, something in me just feels shut off. My daughter can sit right next to me, holding my hand, and I know I love her. I know that. But I can’t feel the warmth of it inside me at all.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things the way you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once liked?

Yes. It’s like I know I should feel something, especially with my daughter right there holding my hand, but I just… don’t. I know I love her, but since my grandson was killed, I can’t feel that warmth or comfort inside me the way I used to.
Has there been anything at all that has brought you joy or pleasure since your grandson passed away?

No… I can’t really think of anything. Even when my daughter sits right beside me and holds my hand, I know I love her, I know I should feel comfort from it… but I just don’t feel that warmth inside me at all. Since my grandson was killed, it’s like that part of me is gone.
Can you describe what happens when you think about your grandson? Do you feel sadness, numbness, or something else entirely?

When I think about him, I just go kind of blank inside. I know I’m sad, I know I loved him, but it’s like I can’t reach the feeling. Even with my daughter holding my hand, I know I love her too, but I can’t feel any warmth from it. It’s just numb.
Has this numbness or lack of feeling been present most of the time, even when you're not thinking about your grandson?

Yes… most of the time. It isn’t only when I’m thinking about him. My daughter can be sitting right next to me, holding my hand, and I know I love her… but I just can’t feel that warmth inside me at all.

Have you noticed that your mood has been consistently low or that you haven’t been able to enjoy things that used to bring you happiness, even outside of moments with your daughter or thoughts about your grandson?

Yes… it’s been like that most of the time. Since my grandson was killed, I just can’t seem to feel good things. Even when my daughter is right beside me holding my hand, I know I love her, but I can’t feel that warmth inside me at all.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day since your grandson passed away?
I… I don’t know if I’d call it depressed exactly. I’ve just felt very empty most of the time. Down, yes, but it’s more like everything is dulled.
Have you found that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or activities, no longer give you pleasure since your grandson passed away?

Yes. I just… I don’t feel pleasure the way I used to. Even with my daughter sitting right there, holding my hand, I know I love her, but I can’t feel that warmth inside me. Everything that should feel good just feels flat.
Have you felt a persistent sadness or emptiness that hasn’t seemed to go away, even when you’re not thinking about your grandson?

Yes. It’s this emptiness that just stays with me. Even if I’m not sitting there thinking directly about my grandson, I still can’t feel warmth or comfort. My daughter can be right next to me holding my hand, and I know I love her, but inside it just feels… blank.
Can you think of any moment, even when you weren’t thinking about your grandson, where you felt genuine pleasure or happiness in something else?

No… I really can’t think of one. Even when I’m not thinking about him directly, there just isn’t any real happiness there. My daughter can be sitting right beside me, holding my hand, and I know I love her, but I can’t feel the warmth of it inside at all.
Even in moments where something good and unexpected happens, like hearing some nice news or seeing a beautiful day, do you find yourself unable to respond with any real happiness or excitement?

Yes… even if something should be nice, I just don’t feel it. Since my grandson was killed, it’s like that part of me is shut off. My daughter can be right beside me holding my hand, and I know I love her, but I can’t feel the warmth of it inside me at all.
Have you noticed that you’re not interested in doing things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or everyday activities, since your grandson passed away?

Yes… I think so. It’s not so much one hobby I can name, it’s just that nothing feels good anymore. Since my grandson was killed, even when my daughter sits right beside me and holds my hand, I know I love her, but I can’t feel that warmth inside at all.
Has there been any activity, even the ones you used to enjoy the most, that has brought you even a little bit of pleasure since your grandson passed away?

No… none that I can think of. Even the things that should mean something don’t really reach me. My daughter can sit right next to me and hold my hand, and I know I love her, but I just can’t feel that warmth inside anymore.
Have you felt a lack of energy or noticed that even small tasks take a lot of effort since your grandson passed away?
I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed it in that way. I’m not doing much, so it’s hard to tell whether small things take more effort or I just don’t feel like doing them.
Have you noticed that nothing at all, not even memories or thoughts that used to make you feel good, bring any sense of pleasure or satisfaction anymore?
Yes. That’s what I mean… since my grandson was killed, even when my daughter is right there holding my hand, I know I love her, but I don’t feel the warmth of it inside. It’s just not there.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation suggests a possible major depressive episode (F32.2) related to bereavement, with persistent inability to experience pleasure (anhedonia) and emotional numbness. Adjustment disorder (F43.12) and prolonged grief disorder (F43.11) are also possible given the recent loss. Recurrent depression (F33.2) remains a candidate if this episode follows prior depressive episodes.

The persistent anhedonia and emotional numbness extending beyond the context of trauma suggests major depressive disorder (F32.2 or F33.2 depending on recurrence) and complicated grief (F43.12). F43.11 (post-traumatic stress disorder, chronic) is ruled out due to absence of re-experiencing, avoidance, or hyperarousal symptoms.
